chronology_note: r145 live-tested a Git Data transaction capsule: two role-local files (text manifest + binary blob) were derived from one stale parent, a deliberate intervening branch advance caused the force=false publish to fail non-fast-forward, and a fresh-parent full-tree rebuild then published both desired blob identities together while preserving the intervening change. This makes the pattern a bounded zero-quota transversal candidate for raw byte writes, atomic multi-file publication, content identity and stale-conflict recovery. Strict boundaries remain: create_blob did not validate malformed base64, arbitrary binary content readback is not byte-faithful in the current connector, and Gmail draft-send ambiguity remains only partially thread-reconcilable. Next: test zero-hosted-compute proof/certificate substitutes for one bounded environment-sensitive compile/test outcome.
